{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Peru|Cuisine of Peru]] 

Peruvian '''''anticuchos''''' are a type of grilled skewered meat, often made with beef heart. The dish is one of the most popular in Peru, and it is often sold by street vendors and accompanied by corn-on-the-cob and portions of cold boiled [[Cookbook:Potato|potato]] with a spot of chili sauce. Those whose tastes do not extend to trying beef heart may substitute any good cut of red meat, though this is not the authentic Peruvian style.

==Ingredients==
* 1 [[cookbook:Beef|beef heart]]
* 2 cloves of [[cookbook:garlic|garlic]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] of ground spicy [[cookbook:chili peppers|red chili]]
* 2 cups of [[cookbook:Vinegar|brown vinegar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] of ground [[cookbook:cumin|cumin]]
* 1 teaspoon of achiote ([[cookbook:annatto|annatto]])
* 1 teaspoon of [[cookbook:salt|salt]] 
* 1 teaspoon of ground [[cookbook:pepper|black pepper]]

==Procedure==
#Place all the above ingredients, other than the heart, in a bowl and mix thoroughly.
#Clean the heart, removing all fat. Cut into bite-sized cubes. Place the heart pieces into the marinade mixture, and leave to marinate for about 10 hours or overnight. The heart should be completely covered by the marinade.
#After marinating, thread the meat onto [[Cookbook:Skewer|skewers]]. If desired, at this stage some additional ingredients such as [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell peppers]] (capsicum) or [[Cookbook:Corn|corn]]-on-cob (cut to a similar size to the heart) may be also added to the skewers. 
#Cook the skewers on a barbecue [[Cookbook:Grill|grill]], turning frequently while brushing with the marinade mix. When the meat is well done, remove skewers from grill and serve immediately.
